Article Title: Moody's chief economist Mark Zandi agrees that AI has been a boon to economic growth, but warns it is also adding to inflation in America by driving up prices of ...
Article Text:
AI is pushing up prices, says Mark Zandi

AI investment dominating the economy

'The bet on AI had better pay off'

Other experts have raised similar concerns

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Read Mark Zandi's complete post here

AI has been a boon to economic growth and job creation, but it's coming with side effects. It’s adding to inflation by driving up electricity and consumer electronics prices, and pushing up interest rates by soaking up capital to finance the AI build-out. It’s also coming at the expense of other investment. Since ChatGPT debuted four years ago, AI has gone from a rounding error to nearly two-thirds of the growth in investment, while growth in everything else has slowed by more than half since mid-2024.

The bet on AI had better pay off in higher productivity, because the rest of the economy isn't investing enough to deliver it.

Mark Zandi, the chief economist at Moody’s Analytics recently said that the rapid rise of artificial intelligence has even a major driver of economic growth and job creation in the United States, but it is also contribution to inflation, higher borrowing costs and decreased investment in other parts of the economy. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Zandi said that the AI investment surge is leading to economic side effects that policymakers and businesses should not ignore. “AI has been a boon to economic growth and job creation, but it's coming with side effects,” Zandi wrote.As per Zandi, the increasing demand for AI infrastructure is leading to inflation by increasing the cost of electricity and consumer electronics. “It’s adding to inflation by driving up electricity and consumer electronics prices,” he wrote. The economist further argued that the huge capital requirements related with building AI infrastructure is also putting an upward pressure on the interest rates. “It’s pushing up interest rates by soaking up capital to finance the AI build-out,” he said. The comment from Zandi comes as the technology companies continue to spend billions of dollars on data centers and the AI computing infrastructure to support generative AI services and applications.Zandi also warned that the AI boom is also growing the crowding out investment in various sectors of economy. As per him, AI-related spending has increased dramatically since OpenAI introduced ChatGPT. Since ChatGPT debuted four years ago, AI has gone from a rounding error to nearly two-thirds of the growth in investment, while growth in everything else has slowed by more than half since mid-2024,” he said. He also suggests that while investments in AI have accelerated, other areas of the economy may still not be receiving enough capital to support broader productivity gains.Zandi concluded his remarks with a warning that the long-term success of the AI boom will ultimately depend on whether the technology delivers meaningful productivity improvements. “The bet on AI had better pay off in higher productivity, because the rest of the economy isn't investing enough to deliver it,” he wrote. His comments reflect growing debate among economists and policymakers over whether the current wave of AI spending will generate returns sufficient to justify the trillions of dollars being invested globally.Peter Schiff recently warned that rising borrowing costs could eventually undermine AI investment and expose broader weaknesses in the economy, while former Federal Reserve adviser Danielle DiMartino Booth has suggested that a recession may already be underway. Meanwhile, Jamie Dimon, CEO of JPMorgan Chase, said in September that AI infrastructure spending could reach $1 trillion in 2027. He estimated that the investment could add about 1% to annual GDP growth, while also potentially contributing to inflationary pressures.The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has also cautioned that weaker-than-expected productivity gains from AI could trigger a pullback in technology investment and lead to a correction in highly valued technology stocks.
Article Summary: Mark Zandi, the chief economist at Moody’s Analytics recently said that the rapid rise of artificial intelligence has even a major driver of economic growth and job creation in the United States. Zandi: “The bet on AI had better pay off in higher productivity, because the rest of the economy isn't investing enough to deliver it”

Article Title: US government is proposing one sentence change in USCIS rules that would change every H-1B visa extension form, with thousands losing their approval
Article Text:
US government is proposing one sentence change in USCIS rules that would change every H-1B visa extension form, with thousands losing their approval

What is the proposed USCIS change

How many visa petitions could be affected

Will H-1B workers lose their visa extensions

How could the change affect workers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has proposed a change to immigration rules that could make it harder for thousands of foreign workers to get their visa extensions approved. The change, one sentence long, would end a rule that requires US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to give weight to its own earlier approval when reviewing an extension request. The change could affect H-1B, L-1, O-1, TN, E and other work visa categories. According to immigration law firm Reddy Neumann Brown PC, the proposal is titled “Removing Deference to Prior USCIS Determinations of Eligibility”. It was published on October 14, 2026. Public comments were due on November 13, 2026.Under the current rule, USCIS generally gives deference to an earlier approval when an employer files an extension for the same worker, job and underlying circumstances. This means the immigration officer usually relies on the previous decision unless there is a major error, a change in circumstances or new information that affects the worker’s eligibility.DHS now wants to remove this requirement by deleting Section 8 CFR 214.1(c)(5) from the rules.If the proposal becomes final, USCIS officers could review an extension application from the beginning, even if the same employer and worker have already received approval for the same job. Officers would still be allowed to consider the previous approval, but they would no longer be required to give it special weight.It must be noted that the change does not mean that all existing visa approvals will be cancelled. Instead, it could make future extension applications more difficult and increase the chances of additional questions or requests for evidence.DHS estimates that around 208,429 petitions filed each year could lose the benefit of deference to earlier approvals. H-1B petitions account for more than 75% of Form I-129 filings, according to the information cited by Reddy Neumann Brown PC. This means H-1B workers are likely to be among the most affected.The impact could be particularly significant for Indian professionals. According to USCIS data cited by the law firm, Indian-born workers accounted for 77.6% of H-1B approvals for continuing employment in fiscal year 2025.The proposed rule does not automatically mean that thousands of workers will lose their approvals. However, it could lead to more extension applications being questioned. USCIS officers could reopen issues that were already reviewed in an earlier application, such as whether a job qualifies as a specialty occupation or whether a worker meets the requirements for the position.DHS estimates that the change could result in around 6,044 additional requests for evidence (RFEs) every year. An RFE asks an employer or applicant to provide more information before USCIS makes a decision.The law firm also noted that DHS’s own analysis found no statistically significant difference in denial rates between periods when deference was applied and when it was not. The measurable impact was an increase in RFEs.More RFEs could lead to longer processing times for visa extensions. This could create uncertainty for workers whose employment depends on receiving an approval before their current status expires.H-1B workers who file an extension on time can generally continue working for the same employer for up to 240 days after their I-94 period expires while the application is pending. Longer processing times could push more cases closer to this limit.The proposal could also affect international travel. Some workers wait for their extension approval before travelling abroad to obtain a new visa stamp. Delays could force them to postpone trips, including travel for family emergencies.Small businesses could face additional challenges as well. DHS data cited by the law firm shows that 57% of employers classified as small entities that filed H-1B extensions in fiscal year 2025 were small businesses. The median small employer filed just one petition.
Article Summary: US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has proposed a change to immigration rules that could make it harder for thousands of foreign workers to get their visa extensions approved. The change, one sentence long, would end a rule that requires US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to give weight to its own earlier approval when reviewing an extension request. H-1B petitions account for more than 75% of Form I-129 filings.

Article Title: Steve Jobs to Jensen Huang, 10 tech founders who were fired from the companies they founded
Article Text:
Jensen Huang, Nvidia

Steve Jobs, Apple

Sam Altman, OpenAI

Elon Musk, X.com (

PayPal

)

Jack Dorsey, Twitter

Travis Kalanick,

Uber

Palmer Luckey, Oculus VR

Jerry Yang, Yahoo

Sam Bankman-Fried, FTX

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Martin Eberhard,

Tesla

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit has put a spotlight on the tech world: founders being ousted from the companies they built. It happens more often than most people think, and Huang is far from the first. Apple founder Steve Jobs Elon Musk and OpenAI ’s Sam Altman were all ousted from the firms they started and built. The reasons vary. Some exits came after minor disagreements or a sharp fall in the share price. Others turned bitter, with CEOs feeling betrayed, filing lawsuits or even being arrested. Here are 10 tech founders who were pushed out of the companies they created.Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO last week (November 12). His exit followed an extramarital affair scandal and a board investigation into concerns that he may have been the subject of a “foreign intelligence effort”. His resignation ends his reign at the chip company he cofounded in 1993. Over 33 years, Huang oversaw Nvidia’s meteoric rise from a scrappy chipmaker to a multitrillion-dollar AI powerhouse.Steve Jobs is one of the most iconic figures in the tech industry, and he co-founded Apple in 1976.Jobs left Apple in 1985, nine years after co-founding it. Slumping sales and Jobs’s demanding management style led to a clash with CEO John Sculley. The board stripped Jobs, who was Apple’s chairman, of his duties, and he resigned. Jobs then founded another computer company, NeXT. Apple acquired it in 1996 for $427 million, and he became Apple CEO the following year. He revitalised it and led it to unparalleled success with the introduction of revolutionary products like the iPhone, iPod, iPad and MacBook.Sam Altman cofounded OpenAI as a nonprofit in 2015 and served as its co-chair alongside Elon Musk. He became CEO four years later and was the face of the AI boom when ChatGPT launched in 2022. In late 2023, the board ousted Altman, saying it had lost confidence in his ability to lead the company and that he was not “consistently candid in his communications.” After employees and investors revolted, Altman was reinstated just four days later.Elon Musk founded X.com as a payments processor in 1999. A year later, it merged with Peter Thiel’s Confinity, which created PayPal. The merged company kept the X.com name at first, with Musk as CEO. Leadership clashed with Musk over the name, his management style and his wish to rewrite the platform’s main infrastructure. While Musk was away, Thiel and his cofounder Max Levchin reportedly organised a letter of no confidence. The board voted to replace Musk and install Thiel as CEO.Jack Dorsey is the only founder who has been pushed out of the same company twice. In 2008, his Twitter cofounder, Evan Williams, fired him as CEO. Dorsey went on to start the payments processor Square. He was brought back to Twitter as interim CEO in 2015, and not long afterward the company dropped “interim” from his title. In 2020, the activist investor firm Elliott Management criticised Dorsey for dividing his attention between Twitter and Square and pushed for his removal. He stepped down as CEO the following year.Travis Kalanick cofounded Uber in 2009 and became CEO the following year. His leadership saw a string of scandals, and the company was criticised for a culture of bullying and misogyny. The New York Times reporter Mike Isaac reported in his book “Super Pumped: The Battle for Uber” that some executives expensed visits to strip clubs.In 2017, Uber lost hundreds of thousands of customers to a viral #DeleteUber campaign. It followed accusations that the company intended to profit from President Donald Trump’s travel ban. After a former engineer, Susan Fowler, alleged harassment and HR failures, Uber launched an independent investigation into its workplace culture. That led to Kalanick’s resignation.Palmer Luckey designed the prototypes for the Oculus Rift virtual-reality headset and raised $2.4 million through a Kickstarter campaign. Facebook acquired his company in 2014 for $2 billion. It is now known as Meta’s Reality Labs division. In 2016, Luckey donated to a pro-Trump group that spread anti-Hillary Clinton memes, which sparked a backlash. He left Facebook the following year. Mark Zuckerberg denied that Luckey was fired for his political views.Jerry Yang cofounded Yahoo as a Stanford student and became its CEO in 2007. Microsoft then offered to buy the company for over $44 billion – a substantial premium on its market value. Yang did not want to sell. After negotiations collapsed, Yahoo’s share price dropped by as much as 20%. The board faced criticism for how it handled the failed deal, and Yang was pressured to resign as CEO.Sam Bankman-Fried became a poster boy for crypto, and his net worth peaked at $26 billion after he founded the crypto exchange FTX. In 2022, CoinDesk reported that his trading firm, Alameda Research, had a balance sheet largely made up of FTX’s own crypto token.Those close ties panicked investors, who rushed to withdraw their money. The exchange did not have enough to cover the withdrawals, partly because of lavish spending by FTX executives. FTX filed for bankruptcy, and Bankman-Fried was replaced by John J. Ray III, an attorney who specializes in recovering funds from failed corporations, including Enron.Martin Eberhard cofounded Tesla in 2003, and Elon Musk joined the company the following year. Eberhard had been CEO since the beginning, but he was ousted in 2007. Reports said that Musk phoned him and said the board had met without him and decided he should step down.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO last week (November 12) His exit followed an extramarital affair scandal and a board investigation into concerns that he may have been the subject of a ‘foreign intelligence effort’ Apple founder Steve Jobs Elon Musk and OpenAI’s Sam Altman were all ousted from the firms they started and built.

Article Title: UpGrad launches advisory arm 'upGrad Next' to help enterprises navigate AI-led transformation
Article Text:
Focus on workforce transformation in AI era

Combining consulting, skilling and hiring

Veteran consulting leaders join

Building an Indian-origin advisory institution

Edtech and workforce development company upGrad has launched upGrad Next, a new enterprise advisory practice aimed at helping organisations redesign their operating models and workforces for an AI-driven future. The company said the new division will bring together advisory services, workforce skilling and talent hiring under a single platform, positioning itself as a one-stop solution for enterprises undergoing large-scale organisational transformation.According to upGrad, the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence across businesses has created a growing need for organisations to rethink how work is structured and how employees are prepared for new technology-driven roles. The company said upGrad Next has been established by a team of senior consulting leaders who have left global consulting firms to build what it describes as an outcome-led, Indian-origin advisory institution. Four leaders have joined as Managing Directors, with additional senior partners expected to join in the coming weeks.upGrad noted that while consulting partners have often launched specialist advisory firms in areas such as tax and mergers and acquisitions, this is the first time in decades that a workforce and HR advisory practice in India is being founded by former partners from leading consulting firms.The company said upGrad Next will advise C-suite executives on organisational and structural transformation while leveraging upGrad's existing ecosystem to deliver employee reskilling, leadership development and recruitment services. upGrad said it worked with more than 700 enterprises during FY26 and plans to use that experience to help companies implement workplace changes more effectively.“The last decade was about digital transformation for organisations. The next decade will be about transforming the workforce to manage, and generate returns from, that transformation,” said Ronnie Screwvala, Co-Founder and Chairperson of upGrad.“Advice, the ability to skill talent at scale, and enablement through AI and technology now need to sit under the same roof. That is what upGrad Next is built to do,” he added.The leadership team at upGrad Next includes Anandorup Ghose, Hrishikesh Godbole, Krishna Chaitanya Malladi, and Dinkar Pawan, all of whom bring extensive experience in human capital consulting, organisation design, compensation strategy and workforce transformation. Ghose, who will serve as Managing Director, previously led rewards consulting practices at Deloitte in India and globally. Godbole is a former EY partner with experience spanning consulting and corporate leadership roles at EY, GE and Godrej.Malladi previously worked in Deloitte's human capital consulting practice, advising organisations on workforce productivity and organisation design, while Pawan brings expertise in HR consulting, economics and executive compensation.Commenting on the launch, Anandorup Ghose, Managing Director of upGrad Next, said businesses would increasingly be judged by their ability to unlock workforce potential rather than simply adopt new technologies. “The next decade won't be won by those who adopt technology fastest, but by those who unlock human potential most effectively,” Ghose said.“Our ambition is to build a world-class, Indian-origin institution that stays accountable for outcomes,” he added. The launch marks upGrad's latest expansion beyond higher education and online learning as it looks to strengthen its presence in enterprise consulting, workforce development and AI-led organisational transformation.
Article Summary: UpGrad Next is a new enterprise advisory practice aimed at helping organisations redesign their operating models and workforces for an AI-driven future. The company said upGrad Next has been established by a team of senior consulting leaders who have left global consulting firms to build what it describes as an outcome-led, Indian-origin advisory institution.

Article Title: Days after DoorDash, Uber said their customers hardly use AI Agents and Amazon banned Meta Muse; OpenAI remains ‘unbothered’, launches ChatGPT's new Wallet
Article Text:
Days after DoorDash, Uber said their customers hardly use AI Agents and Amazon banned Meta Muse; OpenAI remains ‘unbothered’, launches ChatGPT's new Wallet

OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet: How it will work

Amazon bans Meta Muse over ‘safety concerns’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sam Altman-led OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Wallet that lets agents pay without access to users’ actual card details. Built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa, ChatGPT Wallet will initially be available through dots⁠ for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US. In its official announcement, OpenAI said that “with ChatGPT Wallet, we’re now helping people complete purchase, and giving their agents a way to pay that businesses can accept with their existing systems. The announcement comes after Amazon banned Meta Muse and other AI agents from shopping on its platform. Similarly, Uber, DoorDash and Airbnb said that AI agents aren't ‘taking off’.With the ChatGPT Wallet, users can add a card once. They can then approve each purchase without re-entering their payment details. Before each purchase, the user reviews the items, total, and selected card, then approves it with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan.After the user approves, the payment network provides a payment token—a substitute for the user’s actual card details—with a card number, security code, and expiration date. The payment will then be charged to their selected card without ChatGPT Wallet sharing their actual card details with the business or agent.The company says that to accept payment from ChatGPT Wallet, websites need to ensure agents are not inadvertently blocked, and payment and risk systems need to recognize legitimate purchases made by agents.Earlier this month, Amazon blocked Meta's new AI shopping agent, Muse, from buying on its site. Announcing the ban, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said outside shopping bots are not yet worth worrying about. Speaking on the company's earnings call, Andy Jassy said few customers are shopping through outside agents because the experience is still not great and no more convenient than ordering directly from a retailer.The remarks come about a month after Amazon cut off Muse, which Meta rolled out in early September. Users trying to place orders through the agent began seeing an error saying that access by an unauthorised AI agent violates Amazon's Conditions of Use. Amazon cited safety concerns. While Jassy did not name Muse, but the timing made the target clear.Similarly, Uber and DoorDash recently said at their latest earnings calls that they've received hundreds of orders through AI agents like Meta's Muse or Instinct. "It is very, very early, and very limited traction that we have seen so far," Uber CFO Balaji Krishnamurthy said. Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky also revealed that only a negligible portion of bookings on the app are made using AI agents.
Article Summary: ChatGPT Wallet lets agents pay without access to users’ actual card details. Built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa. Will initially be available through dots⁠ for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US. Comes after Amazon banned Meta Muse and other AI agents from shopping on its platform.

Article Title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei once wrote that saying AI will cure cancer is 'more a cliché than it is inspiring'; now, he tells IPO investors cancer will be a 'relic of the past' in ...
Article Text:
Dario Amodei’s cancer promise meets doctors’ doubts

Doctors say curing cancer and Alzheimer's in 10 years is not possible

Anthropic's case rests on WHO work, Claude Science and its own lab

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In August, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei posted on X that saying AI will cure cancer "is more a cliché than it is inspiring, and most people think it is deceptive." The best way to win over sceptics, he added, was to "actually cure cancer. " Three months later, with Anthropic courting investors ahead of its Nasdaq listing, Amodei has made that very promise. In the company's IPO roadshow video, released on November 10, he said cancer, Alzheimer's, heart disease and mental illness will be "relics of the past" in less than a decade. Doctors, including Germany's former health minister Karl Lauterbach, are not buying the timeline."You know, if today we look at things like cancer, Alzheimer's, heart disease, mental illness, these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade," Amodei said. He spoke of an "age of miracles" and tied it to safety, saying the company that gets the risks right will earn "the license to operate that society trusts."Anthropic is seeking a valuation of $1.4 trillion, and its shares are due to start trading on November 19.Lauterbach, a doctor and epidemiologist, responded in German on X on November 11. "It is unclear whether people like @DarioAmodei know so little about medicine or are deliberately misleading the public," he wrote.AI can help with cancer, Alzheimer's and mental illness, he said, but a cure "cannot possibly happen in just 10 years." He wants the focus on prevention.Melinda B. Chu, a doctor and AI medical researcher at Saint Louis University, said Anthropic "has done nothing to suggest they themselves will contribute meaningfully to these goals." Biotech executive Rami Elghandour was blunter about the setting. "I've taken two companies public. These are insane things to say in an IPO pitch," he said.The company's own letter to investors lists "underpromise and overdeliver" among its guiding principles.The same letter makes a softer claim. The seven co-founders wrote that AI could "bring cures for major diseases within reach." The WHO's Regional Office for Africa used Claude during the 2026 Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, cutting its daily situation report from a full day to under an hour. With the Gates Foundation, Anthropic backs free AI clinical search for doctors in about 100 low- and middle-income countries. The founders also say Claude can cut the time to write clinical trial reports "from months to minutes."Its Claude Science beta app for researchers runs analyses and queries more than 60 scientific databases. On the product page, UCSF principal investigator Stephen Francis says it found a lab virus contaminant in his team's RNA-seq data, a problem they had chased for most of a year.The company is building its own biology work too. In October, it bought a one-person biotech start-up working on muscular dystrophy and said it had "begun drug discovery efforts of our own." It reportedly runs a wet lab in the Bay Area.None of this touches the slowest part of medicine. AI can speed up screening molecules and picking drug candidates, but a new drug still has to clear safety, dosing and large efficacy trials in humans before regulators sign off. That part moves at the speed of human biology.Amodei set the bar himself in August. Sceptics will come round when cancer is actually cured, and that is one result no roadshow video can deliver.
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says AI will cure cancer in less than a decade. Doctors, including Germany's former health minister Karl Lauterbach, are not buying the timeline. Anthropic is seeking a valuation of $1.4 trillion and its shares are due to start trading on November 19.

Article Title: A Google datacenter planned on 282 acres in Michigan has moved into construction despite local opposition; the project could use up to 3.6 million gallons of water a day and around one gigawatt of pow
Article Text:
Construction moves ahead after zoning approval

Approvals

Residents push back

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Multi-billion-dollar investment

Google has started construction on a massive hyperscale data centre in Michigan, moving ahead with the project despite months of opposition from local residents concerned about its environmental impact, water consumption and energy demands. According to a report by Mlive, the facility called ‘Project Cannoli’ is planned on a 282-acre site in Van Buren Township near Detroit Metro Airport. The datacenter project is said to become one of the largest investments made by Google in the region. The report further states that the datacenter could consume up to 3.6 million gallons of water per day and need around one gigawatt of electricity when it will become fully functional. This energy consumption of the data centre has raised concerns among the residents, as it will create a lot of pressure on local infrastructure.The development cleared a key hurdle in October when the Van Buren Township Planning Commission voted 5-1 to approve the final site plan. Officials noted that the site was already zoned for industrial use and that planning commissioners were required to approve projects that complied with zoning regulations.The proposed facility will be located between Interstate 94 and Interstate 275, a few miles west of Detroit Metropolitan Airport. The land currently consists of fields, woodland and wetlands. Google will ultimately own and operate the facility, while industrial developer Panattoni is overseeing construction.On October 14, the Van Buren Township Planning Commission voted 5-1 to approve the final site plan after nearly an hour of public comment. The site is already zoned industrial, and the board must approve projects that meet those guidelines. Commissioner Jeff Jahr said the board’s job was to verify the construction is in line with the law. Officials from the township and Wayne County agreed to a $125 million tax break for the project, and county commissioners overrode a veto by County Executive Warren Evans in early October to approve it. The tax break halves local taxes and is worth an estimated $125 million over 12 years. In return, Google will pay the township $15.4 million for local infrastructure and guarantee at least 51 full-time jobs. Google will own and operate the site, and the industrial developer Panattoni is managing construction. Walbridge, a Detroit-based contractor, will build it. Panattoni says the project would bring $2 billion in contracts to Wayne County businesses and 50 to 200 on-site jobs.Residents, especially those in an adjacent subdivision, have objected to noise, utility use and construction impacts. Neighbours say early construction is already affecting them through noise and dust. At the October meeting, resident Maggie Brumar said she hears dump trucks unloading every half hour and can’t keep her windows open because of dust. Others have been angrier. Joe Jones said it was misguided to expect Google to bring benefits to the community.Opposition has also turned political. It has sparked a recall effort targeting the entire township board. Supporters, including the Detroit Regional Partnership, say Google would become the township’s largest taxpayer and pay for public services. Local food pantry operator Mickie Wordhouse said she hoped the project would lead to better public services.Supporters of the project have described it as a once-in-a-generation economic opportunity for the region. Panattoni executives told local officials that construction activities alone would generate about $2 billion in contracts for Wayne County businesses. The completed facility is expected to employ between 50 and 200 on-site workers.Google also received significant local incentives. Wayne County and Van Buren Township approved a tax incentive package worth approximately $125 million after county commissioners voted to override a veto from Wayne County Executive Warren Evans. Google has agreed to contribute $15 million each to the county and township as part of the arrangement. Economic development officials have argued that the arrival of Google could make the company the township's largest taxpayer and generate substantial revenue for local public services.
Article Summary: The facility called ‘Project Cannoli’ is planned on a 282-acre site in Van Buren Township near Detroit Metro Airport. The datacenter project is said to become one of the largest investments made by Google in the region. It could consume up to 3.6 million gallons of water per day and need around one gigawatt of electricity when it will become fully functional.

Intel shareholders have sued the company, accusing it of hiding the impact of a long slowdown in PC sales that led to its stock price falling nearly 29% in a single day, Reuters reports. The lawsuit was filed in a federal court in San Jose, California, by shareholders led by a Michigan pension fund. They claim Intel failed to disclose in time how weak PC sales and excess inventory would hurt its revenue. The shareholders also allege that Intel raised $23 billion by selling shares at $95 each in mid-August, even though the company was already halfway through what they called a “disastrous” third quarter.As stated in the Reuters report, the shareholders allege that Intel's problems with PC sales and excess inventory outweighed ⁠data center construction and other benefits related to the artificial intelligence boom.Intel reported its quarterly results on October 30. The California-based company then projected lower-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue and profit. It also forecasted a prolonged slowdown in PC sales.Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan then told analysts that he was disappointed by manufacturing supply shortages, an "unprecedented memory crunch," and resulting softness in PCs. "We need to ​address these challenges ​with urgency," Tan added.During the earnings call, CEO Lip-Bu Tan said demand for the company’s budget-focused Wildcat Lake chips “is outstripping supply.”CFO David Zinsner confirmed that the chips are now sold out. “We've seen significant growth in Wildcat Lake. It’s coming exactly at the right time because it’s cost-optimized and we’re seeing a lot of focus in that regard,” he said.Wildcat Lake chips are appearing in lower-cost Windows laptops, including the new Dell XPS 13 and HP OmniBook 5 14. These devices are positioned as more affordable options in a market where rising memory costs have put pressure on PC prices.However, some of these laptops start with just 8GB of RAM. That could be a limitation for users who need to run several applications or handle demanding tasks, particularly as Windows laptops can struggle with lower memory configurations.

The lawsuit was filed in a federal court in San Jose, California, by shareholders led by a Michigan pension fund. Samsung has spotlighted its WW12DB8B54GBTL AI-powered washing machine, positioning it as a solution for households managing winter clothing and bulky fabrics. In a statement, Samsung said winter garments such as sweaters, jackets, blankets and bedsheets often require different wash settings, making laundry management more complex. Based on this information, the machine automatically adjusts water usage, detergent levels, soaking duration, rinsing and spinning cycles. Samsung said the technology can reduce detergent consumption by up to 15% while delivering tailored washing performance for different fabric types.The machine also comes with an Auto Dispense system that automatically releases the required amount of detergent and fabric softener for each wash cycle, eliminating the need for manual measurement.Meanwhile, AI Control is designed to learn users' washing habits over time and recommend frequently used programmes, helping streamline day-to-day use.Samsung has equipped the appliance with QuickDrive and Super Speed technologies targeted at users who need quicker washing cycles. According to the company, QuickDrive can reduce washing time by up to 57.5%, while the Super Speed mode can complete a wash cycle in as little as 39 minutes under specified conditions.The WW12DB8B54GBTL also features AI Ecobubble technology, which creates detergent bubbles designed to improve cleaning performance, and Hygiene Steam for deeper cleaning through steam-based wash cycles. Despite a 600mm-wide body, the machine offers a 12kg washing capacity through Samsung's SpaceMax design, making it suitable for larger households and bulky items such as comforters and blankets.The washing machine supports Samsung's SmartThings platform, allowing users to connect and manage the appliance through the company's smart home ecosystem.Samsung said the model is powered by a Digital Inverter Motor backed by a 10-year warranty. Article Title: Apple launches new Health AI study app to understand how people use AI for medical advice
Article Text:
The Apple Health AI Usage Study aims to inform the responsible design of health AI experiences by examining what drives user trust, the quality of responses, comprehension, and everyday health actions. (Image: Apple)

Dedicated app allows users to ask health questions

Apple targets up to 200,000 participants

Privacy and safeguards

Apple has launched the new Apple Health AI Usage Study in the United States. It is a virtual research study and associated app which is designed to advance the understanding of how people interact with conversational health AI tools. “At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life,” said Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness. “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.”As part of the initiative, Apple has released a dedicated iOS app that lets participants ask health-related questions and receive responses grounded in clinical research. Answers are supported by peer-reviewed medical sources, including publications such as The New England Journal of Medicine, JAMA and Nature, according to Apple and OpenEvidence. Users can rate responses and provide feedback on factors such as relevance, detail and usefulness.Participants will also be asked to complete regular surveys to help researchers better understand how AI-generated health information is interpreted and used.Apple is planning to enrol around 2,00,000 adults in the United States for the virtual study. The eligible participants must be at least 21 years old and use an iPhone 15-series device or later running iOS 26 or above. The participants can optionally share the HealthKit data information such as activity, sleep, heart rate and lab results enabling the app to create more personalised responses.The tech giant said that the data will be anonymised before being sent to a secure third-party cloud provider and will not be used to train AI models. OpenEvidence will delete query and response data after 24 hours, according to the company.Apple says the study was designed with privacy protections, transparency and clinical guardrails. Study data won’t be used to train AI models, and participants control whether to share HealthKit metrics or survey responses. The app has safety guardrails meant to detect certain concerning questions and suggest following up with a provider or other resources. Apple stresses that the app isn’t meant to diagnose or treat any condition or replace a medical professional’s advice.
Article Summary: Apple has launched the new Apple Health AI Usage Study in the United States. It is a virtual research study and associated app which is designed to advance the understanding of how people interact with conversational health AI tools. Article Title: Days after resigning over affair, Jensen Huang ‘talks’ return as Nvidia CEO; ‘Everyone loves Jensen’ call, ‘war room’ and more that could bring him back
Article Text:
Jensen Huang eyes Nvidia comeback

Jensen Huang’s allies are building a ‘war room’ to lobby Nvidia’s board

Elon Musk and over 8,000 Nvidia employees have signed the ‘ Bring Jensen Back ’ letter

Washington and Nvidia’s board structure stand in the way of Huang’s return

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jensen Huang is weighing a return as Nvidia’s chief executive, just four days after he resigned from the company he co-founded and ran for 33 years. The former Nvidia CEO has discussed the possibility of a comeback with close confidantes, according to a Financial Times report citing multiple people familiar with the matter. This comes even as an independent probe ordered by Nvidia’s board continues to look into the conduct that led to his exit.Huang stepped down as president, CEO and director on November 12. His resignation followed reports of extramarital affairs with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who has been accused of spying for China, and with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reported directly to him. A report of a third relationship, with another Nvidia employee, surfaced hours after he left. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO, and the $4 trillion chipmaker reports its quarterly results on Tuesday.One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to push for the former CEO’s return. The group will also try to win over the White House, and the effort reportedly has Huang’s backing.“Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen,” the person said.Two large Nvidia shareholders have also left the door open. On Friday, Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker wrote to the board urging it to keep “all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang”.Even his allies aren’t sure how to repair his reputation. “Having an affair with a subordinate is a fireable offence,” one person involved in the effort acknowledged to the FT.The public face of the campaign is an open letter urging the board to “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts”. By Monday morning India time, it carried 169,588 names, with 8,364 identifying themselves as current Nvidia employees. That is close to 20% of the company’s roughly 42,000-strong workforce.The numbers come with a caveat. The campaign itself says affiliations are self-reported and not verified, and reports have flagged entries such as “Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor”.The marquee names are real, though. Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator’s Garry Tan, Shopify’s Tobias Lutke and Replit CEO Amjad Masad are all on the list. Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick wrote that Huang had “erred, yes”, but added, “I do not believe anything he has done rises to the bar of separating him from his company.”Inside Nvidia, an internal suggestion box post asking the board to weigh employee sentiment has drawn more than 1,600 comments, most of them backing Huang. The campaign is also nudging institutional investors to raise the issue on Tuesday’s earnings call at 5pm ET, which is 3:30am IST on Wednesday.Silicon Valley has seen this play out before. In 2023, OpenAI’s board fired Sam Altman and reinstated him within days after staff and investors revolted.In Washington, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that Nvidia should look “outside” the company for its next chief. “They need a dramatic shake-up,” he said in a television interview.He also wants Nvidia to explain within 10 days whether it knowingly let its most advanced AI chips reach China. He called that more important than the affair.Huang has limited leverage inside the company as well. Unlike several other founder-CEOs, he does not hold a controlling stake and cannot overrule the board, the FT noted. The board, now chaired by former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones, has reportedly approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor, though Nvidia said no “formal” process has begun.The Alice Huang angle got murkier over the weekend. Megaspeed, which bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips, said she left the company “effective Aug. 30, 2025” and currently has no role there.Huang and other Nvidia officials have agreed to testify before Congress, though no date has been set. Nvidia and a spokesperson for Huang declined to comment to the FT.In 2023, Huang said he could run Nvidia for another three or four decades. Whether he gets that chance now rests with a board he can’t outvote and a government that wants someone new.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang is weighing a return as Nvidia’s chief executive, just four days after he resigned from the company he co-founded and ran for 33 years. His resignation followed reports of extramarital affairs with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who has been accused of spying for China. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO.

Article Title: In 2016, Priscilla Chan founded a school, 10 years later and after $125 million in donation, Board closed it this year after learning that ...
Article Text:
Funding decision led to the closure of school founded by Priscilla Chan

One of Pricilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg's highest-profile education projects

A ‘whole child’ school

Academic results fell short of expectations

Startup-style approach brought opportunities and challenges

Support package for affected families

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan co-founded a primary school, a tuition-free institution to support low income families via education and healthcare services, has closed after nearly a decade of operations and more than $125 million in funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI) according to a report by The Wall Street Journal. The school, launched in 2016 in East Palo Alto, was designed as an ambitious experiment which combined classroom learning with healthcare, family coaching and other support services which focused at helping children overcome the effects of poverty and trauma. However, the school’s board voted unanimously in April 2025 to close the institution after learning that CZI would not continue funding it beyond the 2025-26 academic year, the report added.As per the WSJ report, the board members decided to shut the school after receiving notice that CZI, the philanthropic organisation founded by Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg, would no longer finance operations beyond the academic year that ended in 2026. Board president Jean-Claude Brizard told the publication that the school's leadership had explored several options for its future, including a gradual wind-down.He said the board would not have approved the closure without alignment from its largest financial backer.A CZI spokesperson told the newspaper that the decision ultimately rested with the school's board, adding that the organisation's focus was on educational outcomes rather than operating costs.The closure comes as CZI has shifted from social issues toward scientific research. Staff were told early last year that funding for social advocacy had been wound down to match its focus as a science philanthropy and the current legal and policy landscape. CZI said there was no evidence that Zuckerberg and Chan attending President Trump’s inauguration influenced the board’s vote. Brizard called the timing an unfortunate coincidence.The closure marks the end of one of the most prominent education initiatives backed by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. In recent years, CZI has increasingly shifted its focus away from social advocacy and education programmes toward scientific research. The Primary School was created to test a model that integrated education, healthcare and family support under one umbrella. Students received services including dental care, developmental screenings and wellness coaching for parents. The school eventually expanded to two campuses and enrolled nearly 540 children.The private, tuition-free school aimed to support the whole child with services such as free dental checkups, early-intervention screenings and wellness coaching for parents. Chan has said her work as a paediatrician showed her that systems for children are often siloed. About three in four students spoke a language other than English at home. Some elements felt closer to a start-up than a school: teachers signed nondisclosure agreements, and some toddlers wore recording devices at home to measure conversations with caregivers for a language programme. Nearly 540 children were enrolled across two campuses. Chan served as co-founder and board chair for about eight years, until 2023.The Wall Street Journal reported that the school's academic performance struggled to meet both state benchmarks and internal expectations, complicating efforts to replicate the model elsewhere. A Stanford University report cited by the newspaper found that 26% of Primary School students in third grade and above exceeded literacy standards in spring 2025, compared with 14% among local students but 47% statewide. At the same time, supporters of the school pointed to achievements beyond academics. School leaders highlighted improvements in student well-being and access to healthcare services. According to the report, about 85% of students received annual well-child visits, well above the rate for children covered by Medicaid in the county.The report also mentioned that the school chose various unconventional practices. The staff worked closely with community clinics to identify high-needs families, while the parents frequently visited campus for coaching sessions and child-development programmes. But the school also witnessed a lot of hurdles such as turnover among principals and difficulties in establishing long-term systems for special education and student discipline. A former employee of the school also told WSJ that building the school's model required more time and planning than initially anticipated.Former consultant Katherine Carter told the publication that launching a school involved far more support and preparation than many people expected.CZI also pledged $50 million after the closure of the school was announced for an easy transition process. The commitment from CZI included support for local community organisations, payment of remaining school lease and education savings accounts for students.The families also received contributions ranging from $1,000 to $10,000 depending on a child's age and programme level, the report said.The WSJ report further states that some of the parents also said that they expected the school top remain a long-term fixture in the community and were disappointed by its closure. However, some also praised the support services it offered. The school officially closed in June, brought an end to a decade-long experiment which sought to reimagine how the schools could support children both inside and outside the classroom.
Article Summary: Priscilla Chan co-founded a primary school in East Palo Alto, California. The tuition-free institution aimed to support low income families via education and healthcare services. Nearly 540 children were enrolled across two campuses. Board voted unanimously in April 2025 to close the institution after learning that CZI would not continue funding it beyond the 2025-26 academic year. School's academic performance struggled to meet state benchmarks and internal expectations.

Bessent made the remarks on Fox News’s Sunday Morning Futures. He suggested that Nvidia’s board should look outside the company for a new leader. Bessent’s comments came soon after he singled out commerce secretary Howard Lutnick for inaction in putting Megaspeed International on a trade blacklist.“As the board conducts a search for a new leader, they need to go outside the company,” Bessent said, as per Bloomberg. He added that what was going on inside Nvidia means the company needs a dramatic shakeup. He also noted he wants to know whether Nvidia deliberately ignored warning signs that shell companies, many of them in Singapore, were sending chips to China. His comments suggest he wants to move attention away from Huang’s personal “foibles” and toward the legal and national-security side of the story.“I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia,” he said, asking whether the company had pushed seemingly illicit sales to boost its revenues and earnings.“I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel,” he said. Bessent said Nvidia has brought in outside counsel. He expects an explanation of what he called a culture of noncompliance at the company.The Treasury chief said he has long supported putting Megaspeed International on a trade blacklist. He pointedly named Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick as the cabinet official who would have to act. “Many other departments were pushing for this, and Commerce had the pen,” Bessent said on Sunday (November 15).Lutnick’s oversight of chip exports and controls has faced growing scrutiny since Huang was ousted from Nvidia on Thursday (November 12). A spokesperson for Lutnick told NBC News last week that he had agreed to testify before Congress.Democrats are eager to hear from Lutnick, as per Bloomberg. Representative Jim Himes of Connecticut, the top Democrat on the House Intelligence panel, spoke on CBS’s Face the Nation. He said it looks as if Lutnick has been the barrier inside the government to stopping the flow of Nvidia chips to China. “And the question is why?” Himes asked. He said it is the Commerce secretary’s job and the president’s job to stop that.Republican Representative John Moolenaar is one of three House committee chairmen seeking testimony from Huang. He said Lutnick and the entire Commerce Department need to answer questions as well.Moolenaar chairs the committee on China’s strategic rivalry with the US. He also suggested Huang should have known that “every Chinese national” can be pressured to spy by the Communist Party. He called that failure “simply irresponsible and a direct threat to our national security.”Lawmakers are pressing Nvidia and the Trump administration for more information on whether they have done enough to keep AI chips out of China. Congress is rallying behind bipartisan export-control legislation that would limit China’s access to AI chips and chipmaking equipment. It could pass within weeks.Bessent rejected calls for such a law, including from Democrats, who will hold majorities in both chambers of Congress from January. “I don’t think we need the legislation. We have all the rules we need. We just need them enforced,” he said.
Article Summary: US treasury secretary Scott Bessent says Nvidia needs a ‘dramatic shakeup’ in leadership after the ouster of CEO Jensen Huang. He also wants answers from the company’s board within 10 days about accusations that the chipmaker helped send advanced AI chips to Chinese entities.
